steps.title: Similarity — lengths and areas
steps.intro: Similar = same shape, different size. Find the linear ratio of one pair of matching lines — everything else follows.

head: What you compare
Ratio
Example (linear \(4:5\))
rows: !Any matching lines — sides, radii, diameters, heights, medians, diagonals, differences of sides

tables.title: Always similar
head: Shape
Why
rows: every circle is the same circle, bigger or smaller
all angles equal, all sides equal
only with the same number of sides

tips: Matching lines = the same kind of line: radius with radius — never a diameter with a chord.
Part vs. leftover: whole \(-\) part first, then the ratio (\(1:25\) whole \(\rightarrow\) \(1:24\) leftover).
Circles on a diameter: their circumferences add up to the big circumference.
Man with glasses: two equal circles on the diameter of a big circle — the top leftover \(=\) one small circle.
NOT always similar: rectangles, rhombuses, isosceles triangles, right triangles — check the angles or both dimensions.

steps.stem: The side length of a regular decagon is multiplied by \(5\). By what factor is its perimeter multiplied?
explanation: A regular decagon with side \(s\) has perimeter \(P=10s\).
With side \(5s\): \(P=10\cdot5s=50s\), and \(\frac{50s}{10s}=5\).
A perimeter is a length, so it changes like the side: \(\times5\). (\(25\) would be the area factor.)

steps.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle with radius \(9\) cm. Six congruent smaller circles have their centers on AB. Their diameters cover AB from end to end, as shown in the figure. What is the sum of the circumferences of the six smaller circles (in cm)?
explanation: Each small diameter is \(\frac16\) of AB, so the ratio of the lengths is \(1:6\). A circumference is a length, so each small circumference is \(\frac16\) of the large one.
Six small circumferences add up to the large circumference: \(2\pi\cdot9=18\pi\).
Check: \(AB=18\), the small radius is \(\frac{18}{12}=\frac32\), and \(6\cdot2\pi\cdot\frac32=18\pi\).

steps.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle. Point C lies on AB, and \(AC=\frac14AB\). A smaller circle has diameter AC. What is the ratio of the area of the smaller circle to the area inside the larger circle but outside the smaller circle?
explanation: The ratio of the diameters is \(AC:AB=1:4\), so the ratio of the circle areas is \(1^2:4^2=1:16\).
Say the small circle is \(1\) unit. Then the whole large circle is \(16\) units, and the region outside the small circle is \(16-1=15\) units.
The requested ratio is \(1:15\). (\(1:16\) is the trap — it compares the small circle with the whole large circle.)

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC, point D lies on AB and point E lies on AC, and \(DE\parallel BC\).
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AD=4\text{ cm} \\ DB=3\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the ratio of the area of triangle ADE to the area of trapezoid DBCE?
explanation: \(DE\parallel BC\), so triangles ADE and ABC are similar. AD matches the WHOLE side AB: \(AB=4+3=7\).
The ratio of the lengths is \(4:7\), so the ratio of the areas is \(4^2:7^2=16:49\).
The trapezoid is the whole triangle minus the small one: \(49-16=33\) units. The requested ratio is \(16:33\).

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, point D lies on BC. The ratio \(BD:DC=2:3\). The area of triangle ABC is \(40\) cm². What is the area of triangle ABD (in cm²)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and ADC are NOT similar, so do not square. They have the same height: the distance from A to BC.
Area \(=\frac{\text{base}\cdot\text{height}}2\), and the height is the same, so the ratio of the areas is the ratio of the bases: \(2:3\).
The whole triangle is \(2+3=5\) units \(=40\), so \(1\) unit \(=8\). Triangle ABD: \(2\cdot8=16\).
(\(6.4=\frac4{25}\cdot40\) is the trap: it squares the ratio. \(24\) is the area of triangle ADC.)

steps.stem:
ABCD is a trapezoid with \(AB\parallel DC\). Its diagonals meet at O.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=4\text{ cm} \\ DC=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
The area of triangle AOB is \(8\) cm². What is the area of the trapezoid (in cm²)?
explanation: Triangles AOB and COD form an hourglass: they are similar, with the ratio \(AB:DC=4:6=2:3\). The ratio of their areas is \(2^2:3^2=4:9\).

Triangle AOD has the same height as triangle AOB (from A to the diagonal BD), and its base OD is \(3\) parts while OB is \(2\) parts. So its area is \(2\cdot3=6\) units. Triangle BOC is also \(6\) units.
In all: \(4+6+6+9=25\) units. Triangle AOB is \(4\) units \(=8\), so \(1\) unit \(=2\).
The trapezoid is \(25\cdot2=50\). (\(26\) forgets the two side triangles.)

steps.title: Similar triangles and rectangles
steps.intro: Prove the match with angles, pair the sides opposite equal angles, then use one factor.

head: Picture
Why similar
What matches
rows: small side \(\leftrightarrow\) the WHOLE big side (\(AD\leftrightarrow AB\), not \(DB\))
small hypotenuse \(\leftrightarrow\) big hypotenuse — sides change places
a side \(\leftrightarrow\) its continuation through the crossing
shared corner, corner on the diagonal

tables.title: Shortcuts
head: Picture
Rule
rows: part to part: \(\frac{AD}{DB}=\frac{AE}{EC}\) — but \(DE\leftrightarrow BC\) (the WHOLE side)
area ratio \(=\) base ratio — do NOT square
four triangles: \(a^2,\ ab,\ ab,\ b^2\) — the side triangles are equal

tips: Make a small–big table: write matching sides one opposite the other.
Rectangles: BOTH dimensions must change by the same factor.
Length ratio \(k\) \(\rightarrow\) area ratio \(k^2\). A trapezoid left over \(=\) whole \(-\) small.
Stuck? Plug in: an easy angle (\(20°\)) to see what matches what, or an easy number that makes a special case and test the choices.

steps.stem: A large cube-shaped box is filled completely with small cubic blocks. The area of one face of the box is \(36\) times the area of one face of a block. How many blocks fill the box?
explanation: Cubes are similar. The ratio of the face areas is \(1:36\), so the ratio of the edges is \(1:\sqrt{36}=1:6\).
The ratio of the volumes is \(1^3:6^3=1:216\). So \(216\) blocks fill the box.
(\(36\) is the area ratio, and \(1296=36^2\) squares the area ratio.)

steps.stem: Each edge of a cube is increased by \(20\%\). By what percent does the volume of the cube increase?
explanation: Turn the percent into a factor: \(+20\%\) means \(\times1.2\).
Volume: cube the factor. \(1.2^3=1.44\cdot1.2=1.728\).
\(\times1.728\) is an increase of \(72.8\%\).

Check with numbers: edge \(10\), volume \(1000\). Edge \(12\), volume \(1728\). The increase is \(728\) out of \(1000\): \(72.8\%\). (\(60\%=3\cdot20\%\) is the trap, and \(44\%\) is the increase of the area of a face.)

steps.title: Similar solids and volume changes
steps.intro: Length, area, volume: power 1, 2, 3 — and for a non-similar change, multiply what changed.

head: Change
Area
Volume
rows: Cone filled to half its height

tips: Similar cylinders or cones: the radius AND the height change by the same factor.
Area ratio \(\rightarrow\) volume ratio: square root first (length), then cube.
Spheres are always similar, like circles and cubes.
Percent \(\rightarrow\) factor \(\rightarrow\) power \(\rightarrow\) back to percent.

steps.stem:
In triangle ABC, point D lies on BC and point E lies on AC, and \(ED\parallel AB\).
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BD=10\text{ cm} \\ DC=15\text{ cm} \\ AE=4\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of AC (in cm)?
explanation: \(ED\parallel AB\), so triangles EDC and ABC are similar (corresponding angles, and the angle at C is shared).
DC matches the whole side BC: \(BC=10+15=25\). The ratio of the lengths is \(\frac{DC}{BC}=\frac{15}{25}=\frac35\).
EC matches the whole side AC. Let \(EC=x\): \(\frac{x}{x+4}=\frac35\), so \(5x=3x+12\) and \(x=6\). Then \(AC=6+4=10\).
Faster (part to part): the parallel line cuts both sides in the same ratio. \(BD:DC=10:15=2:3\), so \(AE:EC=2:3\) too: \(EC=\frac32\cdot4=6\) and \(AC=10\).

steps.stem: ABC is a right triangle with the right angle at C. DECF is a square: D lies on AB, E lies on BC, and F lies on AC. \(AF=5\) cm, and the side of the square is \(x\) cm. What is the length of BE (in cm)?
explanation: \(DF\parallel BC\) and \(DE\parallel AC\), so triangles AFD and DEB have the same angles: they are similar.
Sides opposite equal angles match: AF matches DE, and FD matches EB. \(\frac{AF}{DE}=\frac{FD}{EB}\): \(\frac5x=\frac{x}{BE}\).
\(BE=\frac{x\cdot x}{5}=\frac{x^2}{5}\).
Check by plugging in \(x=5\): both small triangles are isosceles right triangles, so \(BE=5\). Only \(\frac{x^2}5=\frac{25}5=5\) fits.

steps.stem:
ABC is a right triangle with the right angle at A. AD is perpendicular to BC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BD=3\text{ cm} \\ DC=27\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of AD (in cm)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and CAD are similar: both have a right angle at D, and the angle BAD equals the angle C (each is \(90°\) minus the angle B).
Matching legs: \(\frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{DC}{AD}\), so \(AD^2=3\cdot27=81\) and \(AD=9\).
Shortcut: the altitude to the hypotenuse squared equals the product of the two parts: \(h^2=p\cdot q\). (\(3\sqrt{10}\) is the leg AB: \(AB^2=3\cdot30=90\).)

steps.stem: Two concentric circles have radii \(r\) and \(1.3r\). Noah claims that the outer circumference is \(1.3\) times the inner circumference. Emma claims that the area of the ring between the circles is greater than the area of the inner circle. Who is correct?
explanation: Circles are similar. The ratio of the radii is \(1:1.3=10:13\).
A circumference is a length, so the ratio of the circumferences is also \(10:13\): the outer one is \(1.3\) times the inner one. Noah is correct.
The ratio of the areas is \(10^2:13^2=100:169\). The ring is \(169-100=69\) units, and the inner circle is \(100\) units. \(69<100\), so Emma is incorrect.
Answer: Noah only.

steps.stem: D and F are the midpoints of sides AB and AC of triangle ABC. The area of trapezoid DBCF is \(21\) cm². What is the area of triangle ADF (in cm²)?
explanation: A segment that joins two midpoints is parallel to the third side, so triangle ADF is similar to triangle ABC. The ratio of the lengths is \(AD:AB=1:2\).
The ratio of the areas is \(1^2:2^2=1:4\). Small triangle: \(1\) unit. Whole triangle: \(4\) units. Trapezoid: \(4-1=3\) units.
\(3\) units \(=21\), so \(1\) unit \(=21\div3=7\). The area of triangle ADF is \(7\). (\(10.5\) halves the trapezoid, and \(5.25\) takes a quarter of it.)

steps.stem: Two regular hexagons have areas \(150\sqrt3\) cm² and \(30\sqrt3\) cm². What is the ratio of the perimeter of the first hexagon to the perimeter of the second?
explanation: Regular hexagons are similar. The ratio of the areas is \(150\sqrt3:30\sqrt3=5:1\).
Go back from areas to lengths with a square root: the ratio of the sides is \(\sqrt5:1\).
A perimeter is a length, so the ratio of the perimeters is also \(\sqrt5:1\). (Check: the sides are \(10\) and \(2\sqrt5\), and \(\frac{10}{2\sqrt5}=\sqrt5\).)

steps.stem: A hollow glass globe contains a small solid ball. The small ball’s diameter is \(\frac12\) of the globe’s radius. What is the ratio of the difference between their volumes to the small ball’s volume?
explanation: Spheres are similar. Let the globe’s radius be \(R\). The small diameter is \(\frac12R\), so the small radius is \(\frac14R\). The ratio of the radii is \(1:4\).
The ratio of the volumes is \(1^3:4^3=1:64\). Small ball: \(1\) unit. Globe: \(64\) units.
Difference: \(64-1=63\) units. The requested ratio is \(63:1\). (\(64:1\) forgets to subtract.)

steps.stem: A cone-shaped container with base radius \(r\) and height \(h\) is filled with sand using a cone-shaped scoop. The scoop's radius is \(\frac r2\), and its height is \(\frac h6\). How many full scoops are needed to fill the container? (Assume that no sand is spilled.)
explanation: The cones are not similar (the radius and the height change by different factors), so multiply the separate factors.
From the scoop to the container, the radius is multiplied by \(2\), so the volume is multiplied by \(2^2=4\). The height is multiplied by \(6\), so the volume is multiplied by \(6\).
Together: \(4\cdot6=24\). So \(24\) scoops fill the container. (\(12\) forgets to square the radius factor, and \(8=2^3\) treats the cones as similar.)

steps.stem: A map has a scale of \(1:20{,}000\). On the map, the distance between two towns is \(7.5\) cm. What is the real distance between the towns (in km)?
explanation: Scale \(1:20{,}000\): every real length is \(20{,}000\) times the length on the map.
From cm to m, divide by \(100\): \(1{,}500\) m. From m to km, divide by \(1000\): \(1.5\) km.

steps.stem: A map has a scale of \(1:40{,}000\). A lake covers \(5\) cm² on the map. What is the real area of the lake (in km²)?
explanation: First change one map centimeter to kilometers: \(1\) cm \(\rightarrow40{,}000\) cm \(=400\) m \(=0.4\) km.
Areas use the square of the scale: \(1\) cm² on the map is \(0.4^2=0.16\) km² in reality.
\(5\cdot0.16=0.8\) km². (\(5\cdot0.4=2\) is the trap: the scale was not squared.)

steps.title: Map scale
steps.intro: A map is similar to the real land. The scale \(1:n\) is the linear ratio.
tips: Change ONE map centimeter into the unit they ask for first — then square it for areas.
Area trap: multiplying by the scale without squaring.

steps.stem: The ratio of the perimeter of square A to the perimeter of square B is \(\sqrt7:1\). What is the ratio of their side lengths, A to B?
explanation: All squares are similar, and a perimeter is a length.
So the ratio of the sides equals the ratio of the perimeters: \(\sqrt7:1\).

steps.stem: Which of the following rectangles is similar to a rectangle measuring 6 cm × 10 cm?
explanation: The ratio of the sides is \(6:10=3:5\).
Only the \(9\) cm × \(15\) cm rectangle has the same ratio.

steps.stem: D, E and F are the midpoints of the sides of triangle ABC. The perimeter of triangle DEF is \(19\) cm. What is the perimeter of triangle ABC (in cm)?
explanation: Each side of DEF joins two midpoints, so it is half of a side of ABC.
So the perimeter of DEF is half the perimeter of ABC, and the perimeter of ABC is \(2\cdot19=38\). (\(76\) uses the area factor \(4\).)

steps.stem: The area of a circle is multiplied by \(16x\), where \(x>0\). By what factor is its circumference multiplied?
explanation: The area is multiplied by \(16x\), so every length is multiplied by \(\sqrt{16x}=4\sqrt x\).
The circumference is a length, so it is multiplied by \(4\sqrt x\).

steps.stem: A regular octagon with side \(3\) cm has area \(a\) cm². What is the area of a regular octagon with side \(7\) cm (in cm²)?
explanation: Regular octagons are similar. The ratio of the sides is \(7:3\), so every length is multiplied by \(\frac73\).
Areas use the square: \(\left(\frac73\right)^2=\frac{49}{9}\).
The new area is \(\frac{49}{9}\cdot a=\frac{49a}{9}\) cm². (\(\frac{7a}3\) forgets to square.)

explanation: Sectors with equal central angles are similar. The arc lengths give the ratio of the lengths: \(2.5:1=5:2\).
The ratio of the areas is \(5^2:2^2=25:4\).

steps.stem: The area of a square increases by \(96\%\). By what percent does its side length increase?
explanation: Area \(+96\%\) means an area factor of \(1.96\).
The side is a length: \(\sqrt{1.96}=1.4\), so the side increases by \(40\%\).
Check with numbers: side \(10\), area \(100\). New area \(196\), new side \(14\). That is \(4\) more out of \(10\): \(40\%\). (\(48\%\) just halves the percent.)

steps.stem: A cone has volume V. Its radius is multiplied by \(3\), and its height is divided by \(3\). The new cone has volume U. What is the ratio \(U:V\)?
explanation: The radius is multiplied by \(3\), so the volume is multiplied by \(3^2=9\).
The height is divided by \(3\), so the volume is multiplied by \(\frac13\).
Together: \(9\cdot\frac13=3\). The ratio \(U:V=3:1\). (\(1:1\) forgets to square the radius factor.)

steps.stem: At the same time, a vertical pole and a vertical measuring rod \(1.8\) m tall cast shadows on level ground. The rod's shadow is \(2.4\) m long, and the pole's shadow is \(12\) m long. What is the height of the pole (in m)?
explanation: At the same moment, the sun's rays make the same angle with the ground. So the pole with its shadow and the rod with its shadow form similar right triangles.
The pole's shadow is \(12\div2.4=5\) times the rod's shadow.
So the pole is \(5\) times as tall as the rod: \(5\cdot1.8=9\) m.

steps.stem: Points A, B, C, D, E and F lie on one straight line, and \(AB=BC=CD=DE=EF\). Points G and H lie on a ray from A. FG and DH are perpendicular to AF. What is the ratio \(DH:FG\)?
explanation: Triangles ADH and AFG share the angle at A, and each has a right angle (at D and at F). So they are similar.
AD is \(3\) equal parts and AF is \(5\) equal parts, so the ratio of the lengths is \(3:5\).
DH matches FG, so the ratio \(DH:FG=3:5\).

steps.stem: The two right triangles in the figure stand on the same straight line. The marked angle between their neighboring legs is \(90°\). The ratio \(a:b=3:5\). What is the ratio \(c:d\)?
explanation: Let the angle at the shared point inside the small triangle be \(\theta\). The marked angle is \(90°\), so the angle at the shared point inside the large triangle is \(180°-90°-\theta=90°-\theta\).
The large triangle has a right angle, so its third angle is \(\theta\). The two triangles have the same angles: they are similar.
a is opposite \(\theta\) in the small triangle, and c is opposite \(\theta\) in the large one. So a matches c, and b matches d.
Therefore the ratio \(c:d=a:b=3:5\).

steps.stem: Two cities are \(36\) km apart. On a map, they are \(12\) cm apart. What is the scale of the map?
explanation: Change the real distance to centimeters: \(36\) km \(=36{,}000\) m \(=3{,}600{,}000\) cm.
Every map centimeter stands for \(3{,}600{,}000\div12=300{,}000\) cm.

steps.stem: Two maps show the same region. Map A has a scale of \(1:10{,}000\), and map B has a scale of \(1:30{,}000\). A park covers \(18\) cm² on map A. How many cm² does it cover on map B?
explanation: The same real length is \(3\) times shorter on map B (\(30{,}000\) is \(3\) times \(10{,}000\)). The ratio of the lengths (B to A) is \(1:3\).
The ratio of the areas is \(1^2:3^2=1:9\).
\(18\div9=2\) cm². (\(6\) forgets to square.)

steps.stem: \(AB\parallel DE\), and segments AE and BD meet at C. The areas of triangles ABC and EDC are \(7\) cm² and \(63\) cm². What is the ratio \(CD:CB\)?
explanation: The hourglass triangles ABC and EDC are similar. CB (in the small triangle) matches CD (in the large triangle).
The ratio of the areas is \(63:7=9:1\), so the ratio of the lengths is \(\sqrt9:1=3:1\).
So the ratio \(CD:CB=3:1\).

steps.stem: A smaller circle is internally tangent at A to a circle with center O. AB is a diameter of the smaller circle, O lies on AB, and \(OA=5\cdot OB\). What is the ratio of the smaller circle's area to the larger circle's area?
explanation: Let \(OB=x\). Then \(OA=5x\), and the small diameter is \(AB=5x+x=6x\).
The large radius is \(OA=5x\), so the large diameter is \(10x\). The ratio of the diameters is \(6:10=3:5\).
The ratio of the areas is \(3^2:5^2=9:25\), so the answer is \(\frac9{25}\).

steps.stem: A cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base. The smaller cone above the cut has height \(\frac34\) of the original height. What is the ratio of the volume below the cut to the volume of the smaller cone?
explanation: The cut is parallel to the base, so the small cone is similar to the whole cone. The ratio of the heights is \(3:4\).
The ratio of the volumes is \(3^3:4^3=27:64\). Small cone: \(27\) units. Whole cone: \(64\) units.
Below the cut: \(64-27=37\) units. The requested ratio is \(37:27\). (\(64:27\) forgets to subtract.)

steps.stem: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. Chords AC and BD meet at E. The ratio \(AE:DE\) is \(2:3\), and \(AB=8\) cm. What is the length of DC (in cm)?
explanation: The angles ABD and ACD are inscribed angles intercepting the same arc AD, so they are equal (see the circles topic). The angles AEB and DEC are vertical angles.
So triangles AEB and DEC are similar. AE matches DE, and AB matches DC.
\(\frac{AE}{DE}=\frac{AB}{DC}\): \(\frac23=\frac8{DC}\), so \(DC=12\). (\(\frac{16}3\) turns the ratio upside down.)

Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=2\text{ cm} \\ CD=3\text{ cm} \\ AE=(x-1)\text{ cm} \\ EC=(x+3)\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)

steps.stem: A circle is inscribed in a semicircle of radius \(8\) cm. It is tangent to the diameter at its midpoint O and tangent internally to the semicircular arc. What fraction of the semicircle’s area lies outside the circle?
explanation: The circle touches the diameter at O, so its center lies directly above O, at a distance equal to its radius \(r\).
It also touches the arc from the inside, so the distance from O to its center is \(8-r\). Therefore \(r=8-r\), and \(r=4\).
The semicircle: \(\frac{\pi\cdot8^2}{2}=32\pi\). The circle: \(\pi\cdot4^2=16\pi\). Outside the circle: \(32\pi-16\pi=16\pi\).

The fraction is \(\frac{16\pi}{32\pi}=\frac12\). (With similarity: the circle's radius is half the semicircle's, so the circle is \(\frac14\) of the full circle, which is \(\frac12\) of the semicircle.)

Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=8\text{ cm} \\ BC=15\text{ cm} \\ CD=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of AE (in cm)?
explanation: AE and BC are both perpendicular to AB, so \(AE\parallel BC\). AB and CD are both perpendicular to BC, so \(AB\parallel CD\).
So triangles EAB and BCD have the same angles (right angles at A and at C, and corresponding angles at E and at B). They are similar.
AE matches BC, and AB matches CD: \(\frac{AE}{15}=\frac86\), so \(AE=\frac{120}6=20\). (\(11.25\) matches the sides the wrong way round.)

steps.stem: ABCD is a trapezoid with \(AB\parallel DC\). Its diagonals meet at O. The area of triangle AOB is \(4\) cm², and the area of triangle COD is \(25\) cm². What is the area of triangle BOC (in cm²)?
explanation: The ratio of the areas of the hourglass triangles is \(4:25=2^2:5^2\), so the ratio of the bases is \(AB:DC=2:5\).
With bases in the ratio \(a:b\), the four triangles are \(a^2\), \(ab\), \(ab\) and \(b^2\): here \(4\), \(10\), \(10\) and \(25\).
Triangle BOC is \(ab=2\cdot5=10\).

ABC is a right triangle with the right angle at A. AD is perpendicular to BC.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} BD=4\text{ cm} \\ BC=25\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the length of AB (in cm)?
explanation: Triangles ABD and CBA are similar (right angles at D and at A, and the shared angle B). The hypotenuse AB of the small triangle matches the hypotenuse CB of the large one, and BD matches BA.
\(\frac{BD}{AB}=\frac{AB}{BC}\), so \(AB^2=BD\cdot BC=4\cdot25=100\) and \(AB=10\).
Shortcut: \(\text{leg}^2=\text{its part}\cdot\text{hypotenuse}\). (\(2\sqrt{21}\) is AD: \(AD^2=4\cdot21=84\).)

steps.stem: Two rectangles share a corner A, and their sides lie on the same two lines. Their opposite corners B and C lie on the same ray from A, with B between A and C. The ratio \(AB:BC=4:3\). The larger rectangle has area S. What is the area of the smaller rectangle?
explanation: The corner B of the small rectangle is on the diagonal AC of the large one, so the rectangles are similar (a rectangle on the diagonal).
AB matches the WHOLE diagonal AC: \(AC=4+3=7\) parts. The ratio of the lengths is \(4:7\).
The ratio of the areas is \(4^2:7^2=16:49\), so the smaller area is \(\frac{16}{49}S\). (\(\frac{16}9S\) uses the part BC instead of the whole AC.)

ABCD is a rectangle. E lies on the extension of BA beyond A, F lies on the extension of BC beyond C, and E, D and F lie on one straight line.
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AE=4\text{ cm} \\ CF=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the area of ABCD (in cm²)?
explanation: Triangles EAD and DCF each have a right angle (at A and at C). \(AD\parallel CF\), so the angle at D in triangle EAD equals the angle at F in triangle DCF (corresponding angles). The triangles are similar.
Matching legs: \(\frac{AE}{DC}=\frac{AD}{CF}\), so \(AD\cdot DC=AE\cdot CF=4\cdot6=24\).
\(AD\cdot DC\) is exactly the area of the rectangle: \(24\).

steps.stem: ABC is a right triangle with the right angle at B. A circle with radius r is tangent to AB at D and to BC at E, and its center O lies on AC. \(AD=6\) cm. What is the length of BC (in cm)?
explanation: A radius is perpendicular to a tangent, so \(OD\perp AB\) and \(OE\perp BC\). ODBE is a square with side r, so \(AB=6+r\).
\(OD\parallel BC\), so triangles ADO and ABC are similar: \(\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{OD}{BC}\).
\(\frac6{6+r}=\frac r{BC}\), so \(BC=\frac{r(6+r)}6=r+\frac{r^2}6\).

ACF is a right triangle with the right angle at F. AGHJ and CDEF are squares. G lies on AF, B lies on AC, and \(BG\parallel CF\).
Given:
\(\begin{cases} AJ=4\text{ cm} \\ AB=12\text{ cm} \\ BC=6\text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the area of square CDEF (in cm²)?
explanation: AGHJ is a square, so \(AG=AJ=4\).
\(BG\parallel CF\), so triangles ABG and ACF are similar. In triangle ABG, \(AG=4\) is a third of \(AB=12\).
So in triangle ACF, AF is a third of AC. \(AC=12+6=18\), so \(AF=6\).
Pythagoras: \(CF^2=18^2-6^2=324-36=288\). The area of the square is \(CF^2=288\) (no square root needed).
